pull.title: KAFKA-18775: Simplify controller quorum changes through the Admin API
pull.body:
Add convenience Admin APIs that require only a controller ID and extend
the voter RPCs to support deriving omitted directory IDs and endpoints.

Resolve add-voter details from observer state and registered controller
endpoints, and resolve remove-voter directory IDs from the current voter
set. Preserve explicitly supplied voter information.

Update MetadataQuorumCommand to add controllers by ID and make the
directory ID optional when removing controllers. Add Raft, command, and
integration coverage for the new behavior and validation paths.

Reviewers: Luke Chen <showuon@gmail.com>, Kevin Wu <kwu@confluent.io>,
 Chia-Ping Tsai <chia7712@gmail.com>

Hi Luke, thanks for the thorough review and sorry for bringing the misunderstanding...  the goal of this test is to verify the behavior when a user tries to add a voter with an explicit but incorrect directory id.

~~The test intentionally creates two different ReplicaKeys with the same node id but different directory ids. The leader has only seen and caught up one of them as an observer, but the AddVoter request asks to add the other one. Because catch-up is tracked by the full ReplicaKey rather than just the node id, the requested voter is not considered caught up, so AddVoterHandler returns REQUEST_TIMED_OUT[[1](https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/1d953172b99306e5c31982a08a58ecc90130c96d/raft/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/raft/LeaderState.java#L419)][[2](https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/1d953172b99306e5c31982a08a58ecc90130c96d/raft/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/raft/internals/AddVoterHandler.java#L294)].~~

~~Update:
So this test verifies that the current implementation does not overwrite or derive the directory id when the user provides one explicitly. Instead, it preserves the user-provided ReplicaKey and passes it through to AddVoterHandler. As before, an incorrect explicit directory id means the requested voter cannot be matched to the caught-up observer, and the request times out.~~
I'll add more comments in the test, hope it helps

review_comments.body: This change makes sense. @brandboat , please also reply to the KIP-1141 discussion thread for this minor update.

@showuon, I checked the behavior for directory ID and endpoint mismatches.

For a directory ID mismatch:
- If the controller endpoint is correct but the directory ID is wrong, the request is treated as “lagging behind.” This is because a ReplicaKey is composed of `controllerId + directoryId`. The real observer has fetched using its actual directory ID, but the request uses a different directory ID.  Since the leader has no fetch/catch-up state for that exact ReplicaKey, Kafka treats it as a different replica that has not caught up yet.

For an endpoint mismatch, it's a bit tricky:
- If the endpoint is completely wrong or unreachable, AddVoterHandler sends an `API_VERSIONS` request to that endpoint, the request fails, and AddVoter fails. 
- If the endpoint is reachable but points to another controller, AddVoter may still succeed. The endpoint is used for the API_VERSIONS probe, while voter catch-up is checked by ReplicaKey, not by endpoint ownership. This can be self-healing. After the target controller becomes a voter, KafkaRaftClient can detect that its local endpoint does not match the latest voter set and send UpdateVoter. The leader can then persist a corrected VotersRecord. This endpoint update mechanism is part of [KIP-853’s UpdateVoter flow](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/spaces/KAFKA/pages/217391519/KIP-853%2BKRaft%2BController%2BMembership%2BChanges).

It would be good to document this behavior for the below cases in the PR description. I see it in the KIP: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/spaces/KAFKA/pages/340037949/KIP-1141+Simplifying+Add+Remove+Voter+in+MetadataQuorumCommand#KIP1141%3ASimplifyingAdd%2FRemoveVoterinMetadataQuorumCommand-Serversidechanges.

- AddRaftVoter v2 and the `voterDirectoryId` is specified, but the `endpoints` is not.
- AddRaftVoter v2 and the `endpoints` is specified, but the `voterDirectoryId` is not.
- AddRaftVoter v2 and both `endpoints` and `voterDirectoryId` are specified.
- RemoveRaftVoter v1 and `voterDirectoryId` is specified.

From reading the code here, it seems like if these fields are specified in the request, that takes precedence in AddRaftVoter v2 and RemoveRaftVoter v1, and only if they are empty/not present, do we default on what the `nodeProvider` says. This behavior seems reasonable to me, but we should document it because it is not clear without reading the code.
This test needs to be updated after my other suggestion. It may be easier to just check the exception class type.
I think this needs to be updated to 4.5.

```suggestion
                        "observer remained active. Remove stale or inactive observer entries so that " +
```
Maybe it is worth printing for how long the old incarnation of the node remains an active observer by printing:
```
OBSERVER_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS - (currentTimeMs - integerReplicaStateEntry.getValue().lastFetchTimestamp)
```
Also, there is no way to remove the observer entry in the leader state. The only way to clear this is to wait for the observer session to expire or the leader to change and the new node to fetch from it (assuming the old incarnation does not fetch to the new leader too).

Also, it would be nice if we could add a unit test case for this scenario, mainly to ensure the active controller does not remain in a state where it cannot add this node's voter id when there are multiple matching observers. 

Here is what the test could look like at a high level:

- The test would set up the local node as the leader. 
- Deliver a fetch from the "old" node incarnation.
- Deliver a fetch from the "new" node incarnation. This represents the old node getting its log replaced and re-fetching.
- Try `AddRaftVoter` v2. This should fail with this exception.
- Advance time to expire the observer session of the old node.
- Try `AddRaftVoter` v2. Now the request succeeds.
Why do we need this annotation? Is it because it is using a deprecated method? Can we instead make the call to `admin.remove/addRaftVoter` use the updated methods?

More of a high level question, but why not put these tests in `ReconfigurableQuorumIntegrationTest`? That file seems more appropriate to me. It seems the purpose of these tests are to test that the `--bootstrap-controllers` flags works for CLIs. Meaning, that when clients send requests to the brokers, forwarding them to the controller vs sending the request to the controller directly should not change the behavior of the request.

I think the `kafka-metadata-quorum` CLI is already covered by the `testDescribeMetadataQuorum` test above right?

Should these flags be mutually exclusive? Meaning, is the below a valid invocation:
```
kafka-metadata-quorum add-controller --bootstrap-server <> --controller-id 1 --command-config <>
```
In the current code, you will run `handleAddControllerById` and ignore the second flag.

commit.message:
KAFKA-18775: Simplify controller quorum changes through the Admin API

Add convenience Admin APIs that require only a controller ID and extend
the voter RPCs to support deriving omitted directory IDs and endpoints.

Resolve add-voter details from observer state and registered controller
endpoints, and resolve remove-voter directory IDs from the current voter
set. Preserve explicitly supplied voter information.

Update MetadataQuorumCommand to add controllers by ID and make the
directory ID optional when removing controllers. Add Raft, command, and
integration coverage for the new behavior and validation paths.
Add options and deprecate original add remove raft voter methods

rename.to: KAFKA-18775: Simplify controller quorum changes through the Admin API

timeline.message:
KAFKA-18775: Simplify controller quorum changes through the Admin API

Add convenience Admin APIs that require only a controller ID and extend
the voter RPCs to support deriving omitted directory IDs and endpoints.

Resolve add-voter details from observer state and registered controller
endpoints, and resolve remove-voter directory IDs from the current voter
set. Preserve explicitly supplied voter information.

Update MetadataQuorumCommand to add controllers by ID and make the
directory ID optional when removing controllers. Add Raft, command, and
integration coverage for the new behavior and validation paths.
